# Q3 Access Review - Completed

**Completed:** 2026-10-10 · **Procedure:** Access Review Procedure · **Working tracker:** Q3 Access Review Tracker · **Result:** all 20 systems reviewed and signed. Completed 10 days after quarter end; documented as an exception below.

This closes gap 1 from SOC 2 Readiness Review - September.

## Final numbers

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Systems reviewed | 20 of 20 |
| Accounts reviewed | 383 |
| Accounts removed | 25 |
| Accounts reduced | 5 |
| Local (non-SSO) accounts found | 2 (both removed) |
| Accounts with evidence of inappropriate use | 0 |

## Last six systems (closed Oct 9-10)

| System | Owner | Removed | Reduced | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plaid dashboard | Marcus | 1 | 0 | KYC migration contractor |
| Lithic dashboard | Marcus | 0 | 0 | Sandbox only; 4 users |
| PagerDuty | Marcus | 1 | 0 | Former contractor still on an escalation policy |
| Snowflake | Devon | 2 | 1 | One local account from a 2025 data export job; one analyst reduced from admin |
| Customer.io | Kavi | 0 | 0 | |
| Branch | Nadia | 0 | 0 | |

Plus the Tier 1 summary sign-off by Maya Chen, which she gave on Oct 10 instead of Oct 12.

## Notable findings across the quarter

1. **Cut-over leftovers.** A Pillar Bank portal login and elevated Postgres write access both created for the ACH cut-over were never removed. Both cleaned up. Going forward, any temporary access for a project gets an expiry date at grant time.
2. **GitHub outside collaborators.** 3 former contractors with read access to the monolith. Offboarding workflow now covers outside collaborators.
3. **Local accounts.** 2 found (Pillar portal, Snowflake). The local-account check added after the Type I worked.

## Exception: late completion

- **Control:** quarterly access review completed by quarter end.
- **What happened:** Q3 review started Sep 21 instead of Sep 1 and completed Oct 10, 10 days late.
- **Why:** system owners (mainly Marcus Bell and Devon Park) were committed to the Sep 26 incident response, the Pillar follow-up and the investing GA blockers. I started the window late.
- **Impact:** none found. No inappropriate access was discovered for the late period.
- **Remediation:** Q4 review runs Dec 1-31 with Tier 1 systems first. Backup system owners named for Marcus's Tier 1 systems (Sarah Kim for Postgres and the Pillar portal). Calendar holds sent to every owner today.

Decision: this exception goes into the Type II evidence folder as-is and is mentioned in the SOC 2 status letter to Northfield. No softening.

## Evidence filed

- Exports for all 20 systems, timestamped
- Owner decisions per account
- Remediation proof (second exports)
- Owner and Tier 1 sign-offs
- This exception memo

## Remaining SOC 2 readiness gaps

- MDM: 65 of 68 laptops, due 2026-10-17 (MDM Rollout Plan)
- Vendor risk assessments: Alloy and Customer.io, due 2026-10-24

## Actions

- [x] Sam: complete Q3 access review by 2026-10-10
- [x] Maya: sign Tier 1 summary by 2026-10-12
- [ ] Sam: send the updated access review line to Maya for the SOC 2 status letter by 2026-10-11
- [ ] Sam: Q4 access review calendar holds confirmed by all owners by 2026-10-16
- [ ] Marcus: reduce production database direct access from 4 people to 3 by 2026-10-23
